newsitem.title: FRANCE: U.S. court orders Parretti to pay $1.5 billion.
newsitem.headline: U.S. court orders Parretti to pay $1.5 billion.

text.p: Italian fugitive financier Giancarlo Parretti has been ordered by a U.S. court to pay $1.5 billion in damages over his 1990 purchase of Hollywood studio MGM, a French state holding company said on Tuesday.

The court ruled that Parretti, who is on the run from U.S. justice authorities, must pay the money to the CDR holding company, which took over the loan granted by French bank Credit Lyonnais to Parretti to buy the studio.
The Consortium de Realisation (CDR) said Parretti had been ordered by the Superior Court in Los Angeles to pay the money for fraud in the purchase of MGM and for "looting the studio."
In February, Parretti forefeited $25,000 bail after failing to return from Italy for sentencing in Delaware on a conviction of perjury and evidence tampering that carried a maximum 10-year penalty.
Last March, the California court dismissed Parretti's $3.9 billion lawsuit against Credit Lyonnais for foreclosing on his loan to buy the studio.
CDR said the court ordered Parretti to pay $1.1 billion in damages and around $376 million in interest.
